question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations Using Standard Gaussian Elimination with Row Exchanges
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

question.knowledge_point: Finding the Parametric Representation of an Affine Transformation Given its Matrix Form
question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=au+bv+3,\,y=-9u+cv+4
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 4\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -9 & 4\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u \\ -9u+4v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}u+3 \\ -9u+4v+4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=1u+0v+3,\,y=-9u+4v+4
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=1+0+4=5.
$$

question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=au+bv-2,\,y=u+c
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

We can carry out the matrix operations using the matrix form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 & 8 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}}\cdot \overset{u}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}}+\overset{b}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u+8v \\ u\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u+8v-2 \\ u+5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding elements, we obtain

$$
x=6u+8v-2,\,y=u+5
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=6+8+5=19.
$$

question.problem:
The matrix form of the affine transformation

$$
x=-5v-2,\,y=7v-2u-3
$$

is shown below. What is the value of $a+b+c?$

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & a \\ -2 & b\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}c \\ -3\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

First, notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-5v-2 \\ 7v-2u-3\end{aligned}].
$$

Separating the constants and expressing the linear part as a product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-5v-2 \\ 7v-2u-3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5v \\ -2u+7v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 \\ -2 & 7\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=-5+7+(-2)=0.
$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}6u-v \\ 2u-3v+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6u-v \\ 2u-3v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}6 & -1 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}.\end{aligned}

question.knowledge_point: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System
question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 8 & 16 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x+2y=-1 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+2y=-1.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-1-2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-1-2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1-2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a Singular 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination
question.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y=4 \\ -3x+6y=-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system.
question.worked_solution:
First, we set up the augmented matrix for the system:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & 6 & -12\end{aligned}]
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ -3 & 6 & -12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x-2y=4 \\ 0x+0y=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-2y=4.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=4+2y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=4+2y \\ y=y\end{aligned}
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4+2y \\ y\end{aligned}],\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

No submitted grades are supplied; confirmation rests on the worked solutions. q-124301: coefficient comparison gives a=6, b=-3, c=4, so the sum is 7. q-20963: R2←R2−8R1 yields rows (1,2,-1) and (0,0,0), so x=-1-2y with y arbitrary. q-73740: R2←R2+5R1 gives the same echelon form and solution; the source's omitted comma in its vector notation does not change the answer. q-73750: R2←R2+3R1 yields rows (1,-2,4) and (0,0,0), so x=4+2y with y arbitrary. q-130923: R2←R2+4R1 yields rows (1,-2,-1) and (0,0,3); the contradiction 0=3 proves there is no solution. q-91033: y'=-sin(x) and y''=-cos(x), giving 2sin(x)-cos(x). q-337831: y'=3cos(3x) and y''=-9sin(3x), giving -14sin(3x)+6cos(3x). q-65037: y'=1/x and y''=-1/x², so xy''+2y'=1/x for x>0. q-91045: y'=4x³, y''=12x², and y'''=24x; the cubic terms cancel, leaving 4x⁴. q-337848: y'=2x and y''=2, so D(y)=(x²+1)(2-2x²+5)=(x²+1)(7-2x²). q-338254: y'''=-8cos(2x), so xy y'''+3y=sin(2x)(3-8xcos(2x)). q-130930: the nonzero rows lead in columns 1 and 3. q-130935: they lead in columns 1, 3, and 4. q-35391: pivot columns are 1, 2, 4, and 5, leaving column 3 as the sole non-pivot column. q-130955: pivot columns are 1, 2, and 4, again leaving column 3. q-130962: R2←R2−R1 and R4←R4+2R3 produce leading entries in columns 2, 3, 5, and 6, hence four pivot columns.
